question: Does ranking for locality starve the node it ranks last, and does an expiry deadline fix it without taking over?

versions.ffmpeg: ffmpeg version 2025-02-06-git-6da82b4485-full_build-www.gyan.dev Copyright (c) 2000-2025 the FFmpeg developers

notes: synthetic: no footage, a fetcher charging 2 ms a frame and nothing else. What is measured is which declaration the scheduler picks; a real decoder would lay a seek/step distribution over an effect that is about ordering.

topology: one ORDERED node arming 60 rows at once at DEFERRED, against a person scrubbing without pause — a 40-row INTERACTIVE declaration re-stated every 20 ms at a new position, so it is always unserved and always outranks. 3.0 s per arm.

prior art: the subsumption rule this starves under is anticipatory scheduling (Iyer & Druschel, SOSP 2001); the expiry queue that repairs it is the deadline family's anti-starvation half, drained in a batch after `fifo_batch`.
arm no deadline: the ordered node computed 1 of 60 armed rows; the expiry queue made 0 of 995 picks (0.0).
arm deadline 0.3s: the ordered node computed 60 of 60 armed rows; the expiry queue made 59 of 1058 picks (0.0558).
result: 1/60 rows without a deadline against 60/60 with one, and the expiry queue took 0.0558 of picks doing it — a floor under service, not a replacement for the ranking.

cases.name: deadline-0.3s
cases.note: expiry measured against last service, drained in a batch
